items.title: 3D editor, `ctrl` remains pressed after closing (`ctrl s`) `Save Scene As...` window
items.body:
### Godot version

v3.5.beta2.official [7a4f9dfb1], v3.4.4.stable.official [419e713a2]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

In the 3D editor. The `ctrl` key remains pressed,
after closing a window, that was opened with a `ctrl` shortcut.
For example: `ctrl s` (`Save Scene As...`) or `ctrl a` (`Create New Node`)

**Workaround**: Press and release the `ctrl` key once.

It happens when the window is closed by:
- pressing `enter` to accept the file name or the selected node
- `left` mouse clicking on the `cancel` button, top right `x` button, or outside the window

It doesn't happen when:
- the window is closed with `esc`
- the `Save Scene As...` window was opened from the menu: `Scene > Save Scene`
- the `Create New Node` window was opened from the Scene dock's `Add Child Node` button

This was discovered when the 3D editors `Use Snap (Y)` button,
seemed to become reversed after saving a new scene with `ctrl s`.

This issue doesn't seem to happen in the 2D editor.

### Related issue
There's a related issue where the `ctrl` key remains pressed when pressing `ctrl alt tab`:
"Use snap" button with "snap to grid" has inverted effect #26968

The issue is closed, but KoBeWi's comment https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/26968#issuecomment-490516437 still applies.
>I just found a way to reproduce it. Hold Control to invert snapping and press Alt + Tab. When you focus Godot again, the Control will be "stuck" until you press it again

The issue was closed as a duplicate of:
If you alt-tab off and in the editor and you drag a sprite it will act like if alt were pressed #12592

But the duplicate is only referring to the `alt` key remaining pressed.

The duplicate issue was closed after someone was unable to reproduce it in Linux.
The third from the last comment https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/12592#issuecomment-558611903 asked if it's reproducible in Windows.
I'm unable to reproduce the duplicate (`alt`) issue in Windows in either Godot 3.5.beta2, or 3.4.4.

But since the `ctrl alt tab` issue, still is reproducible:
"Use snap" button with "snap to grid" has inverted effect #26968

Then it probably should be reopened.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new scene
- Click on the button: `3D Scene` to add a `Spatial` node
- Make sure that the `Use Snap (Y)` button is disabled (above the viewport)
- In the 3d viewport, move the `Spatial` node by dragging the red arrow.
Observe that the node moves by decimal values. It doesn't snap (as expected).
- Now press `ctrl s` to open the `Save Scene As...` window
- `Left` mouse click on the `Cancel` button
- In the 3d viewport, move the `Spatial` node by dragging the red arrow.

### Expected
Dragging the red arrow shouldn't snap, because the `Use Snap (Y)` button is disabled.

### Observed
Dragging the red arrow now snaps to integer values.
Even though, the `Use Snap (Y)` button is disabled.

The same thing happens in reverse if the `Use Snap (Y)` button was enabled,
before the `ctrl s` (`Save Scene As...`) window was opened.

### Workaround
Pressing and releasing `ctrl`, restores the expected behavior.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_

### Godot version

### Issue description

I am working with some CSGPolygon3Ds, which follows paths that change sometimes.

For optimization purposes, it gets converted to a MeshInstance whenever the path isn't supposed to change. To do so, the CSGPolygon3D child is removed and a converted MeshInstance is added.

### Godot version

v4.1.dev2

### Issue description

Closing the editor after building a C# project prints these errors:

```
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from '@ConfirmationDialog@16952:<ConfirmationDialog#1125499591109>'. Signal: 'confirmed', callable: 'Delegate::Invoke'.
   at: (core\object\object.cpp:1353)
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from '<VBoxContainer#1125902244315>'. Signal: 'ready', callable: 'Delegate::Invoke'.
   at: (core\object\object.cpp:1353)
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from '@Button@16961:<Button#1126405560822>'. Signal: 'pressed', callable: 'Delegate::Invoke'.
   at: (core\object\object.cpp:1353)
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from '@PopupMenu@16960:<PopupMenu#1126036462051>'. Signal: 'id_pressed', callable: 'Delegate::Invoke'.
   at: (core\object\object.cpp:1353)
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from '<EditorSettings#-9223372008903932771>'. Signal: 'settings_changed', callable: 'Delegate::Invoke'.
   at: (core\object\object.cpp:1353)
```

### Causes and possible fixes

Reloading the managed assemblies causes the hash of `ManagedCallable` instances to change, corrupting the hash map of signals and causing these issues on cleanup.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/75533 prevents the GodotTools assembly from being reloaded and thus prevents these errors in particular, but these errors will still trigger when using custom editor plugins.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take any C# project (the project must have the solution, but no C# code is required)
2. Rebuild the solution
3. Exit the editor

So either make the reason for this specific error message crystal clear, or make the "Unexpected token" error message in general more clear.

**Elaboration**: Comprehensible error messages are very important for programming. Personally, I tried Godot Engine and GDScript for the reasons mentioned above, then got this bizarre error even when following basic, community-approved programming tutorials. For instance, I followed this tutorial by GDQuest (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UcdwP1Q2UlU ), and copying the code on most of the slides in that video causes the error mentioned in this issue, unless you code inside a function like _ready. items.title: StyleBoxFlat downscaling corner radius causes incorrect rendering with border width and anti-aliasing set
items.body:
### Godot version

4.0.beta4

### System information

macOS 12.6.1

### Issue description

A StyleBoxFlat (and possibly other StyleBox types) with corner radius set will downscale the corner radius if they are too large to fit. For example setting a 20px radius on all corners and scaling the box to be just 30px wide will result in 15px radius corners. This is useful since you can then basically make Styleboxes that are round or have rounded ends at any size < 2*the corner radius. 

The issue is that as you can see this downscaling doesn't work correctly if you have a border width set for the StyleBox. It seems this messes up the downscaling size calculation somehow, so the middle vertices become misaligned, resulting in graphical artifacts. Especially if you have alpha blending on the BG Color:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17763524/201317258-5d6274e6-8095-4359-97f0-2822f3c34756.mov




### Steps to reproduce

Setup:
- Create a Panel in a new 2d scene
- Set the panel to use a new StyleBoxFlat ThemeOverride style
- Set the BG Color to be a semi-transparent color
- Set a border width on all sides (larger like 5 for more obvious result)
- Set a corner radius on all corners (larger like 20 for more obvious result)

- Now, resize the Panel and observe an overlap appear in the middle as described above if the panel is made smaller than 2xCorner radius so downscaling of the radius is applied.

### Minimal reproduction project

See steps to reproduce, should work in any project?

items.title: Joystick Navigation broken for OptionButton
items.body:
Using the new Godot v3.2 release, with Ubuntu 18.04.3 LTS

I've been messing around with 3.2, and I noticed that I can now assign Joy Axis inputs to the ui_left/right/up/down actions, and for the most part the menu navigation works as expected. Pushing a direction on the joystick only moves the selection once until the joystick position is reset, which seems like the expected behavior to me (whereas in the last version of Godot the selection would jump every single time the joystick moved at all). 

However, I still notice a problem when I use an OptionButton, where after I select it and move the joystick, it retains the problematic behavior from before where any slight movements cause the selection within the OptionButton menu to jump. To me, the expected behavior would be for the selection to only move up or down the first time the joystick is moved up or down, until its position is reset, just like with other UI navigation. I suspect that this problematic behavior may occur in other UI elements too though I haven't checked yet.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create a new project
2. Modify the Input Map by adding `Device 0, Axis 0 - (Left Stick Left).` to ui_left, etc. for all 4 ui directions
3. Create a new Control scene, add a container, then add an OptionButton to that container
4. Add a number of items to the OptionButton
5. (Optional) Add a script to the control to grab the focus of the OptionButton on _ready
6. Run the project, then use a controller (I used an XBox One S controller) to click on the OptionButton
7. Move the joystick up and down to see how the selection jumps too quickly

Sample project (includes one of each button type): 
[JoystickUITest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4135469/JoystickUITest.zip)

I did notice some other focus problems in that sample project, but I can go ahead and create new issues for those if needed (to summarize, MenuButtons and LinkButtons aren't focused when navigating past them, even if they are explicitly defined as neighbors).
